comparison: Both evaluate expansion of immature neutrophils (C3, C4, C42, C43) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes diagnostic performance claims (C46-C49, C67) and correlations (C44-C45) which peer reviewers accepted without challenge. Strong agreement on the novel finding of immature neutrophil mobilization.

OpenEval R1 includes correlations with cardiac function (C44, C45) that overlap with peer R2's acceptance of correlations (C44, C45, C61, C62). Both find these correlations SUPPORTED, though peer review implicitly accepts them while OpenEval explicitly validates them.

OpenEval R1 includes diagnostic performance claims (C46-C49, C67) that peer R3 questions with UNCERTAIN evaluation. Peer reviewers requested analysis of whether combined parameters improve ROC values, indicating uncertainty about added diagnostic value that OpenEval rated as SUPPORTED.

Both address correlations with cardiac markers. OpenEval finds neutrophil correlations (C61-C62) SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of understanding white blood cell activation. Agreement on correlation data validity.

OpenEval finds diagnostic performance (C63-C66) SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting analysis of whether combined parameters improve diagnostic value. Disagreement on whether diagnostic utility is adequately demonstrated.

Perfect claim overlap (C11, C12, C79, C80) on gene expression data. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on RT-qPCR methodology, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to lack of rationale for specific gene selection. Disagreement on whether gene selection is adequately justified.
Perfect claim overlap (C13, C97, C98) on apoptosis resistance. Both find SUPPORTED with no challenges raised. Strong agreement that apoptosis data using multiple methods is convincing.

OpenEval addresses lack of T-cell suppression (C53, C54) as part of functional characterization rated SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also accept this finding (C19, C53, C54) as SUPPORTED. Agreement on T-cell proliferation assay results.

Both address macrophage differentiation and cytokine production (C55-C58). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on multiple complementary assays, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, concerned about overinterpretation of in vitro data and lack of in vivo validation. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

OpenEval addresses gene expression (C50, C51) as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers question gene selection rationale (UNCERTAIN). Similar concern as with neutrophil genes - disagreement on whether gene choices are justified.
Both address T-cell proliferation (C19). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on assay appropriateness, peer reviewers also accept as SUPPORTED. Agreement on this negative result.

Both address macrophage differentiation (C20). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about in vitro limitations and overinterpretation. Disagreement on strength of conclusions from in vitro data.

Both address CMV associations (C14, C148-C152). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on statistical associations and PCA, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the mechanistic link between CD28null cells and neutrophil effects. Disagreement on interpretation of CMV-related findings.

Partial overlap on bioinformatic associations (C16, C17, C154-C158). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through multiple analytical approaches, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with concerns about mechanistic connections and physiological relevance. Disagreement on interpretation.

Both address neutrophil-T cell interactions (C18, C159-C165). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on transwell experiments and neutralization, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning physiological relevance, location of interactions, and plasma IL-12 levels. Disagreement on in vivo relevance.

Both address cell-type specificity (C168-C170). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on differential responses, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns about neutrophil-T cell interaction mechanisms. Partial disagreement on interpretation.

Both address CMV independence of neutrophil phenotype (C167). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, peer reviewers include this in UNCERTAIN evaluation, asking whether neutrophils from CMV+ vs CMV- patients differ functionally. Disagreement on completeness of characterization.

Both address mouse model neutrophil trafficking (C21, C22, C128-C132, C172, C173). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of species differences, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting bone marrow data, absolute numbers, and discussion of neutrophil fate. Disagreement on completeness of mouse data.

Both address apoptosis resistance in mouse neutrophils (C133, C134). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as cross-species validation, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns about mouse model characterization and neutrophil fate. Partial disagreement.

Both address neutrophil presence in lymphoid organs (C138-C142). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with caveat that function is speculative, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning neutrophil fate and maturation in tissues. Agreement that presence is shown but function uncertain.

Both address CD101 as mouse maturation marker (C82, C83, C86). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on RNA-seq and validation, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether CD101 reflects immaturity vs activation. Significant disagreement on marker validity.

Both address bone marrow depletion (C87, C88). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable inference, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting bone marrow level data. Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Perfect claim overlap on mouse gene expression (C89-C94). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, asking if CD101- specific analysis would show more similarities to human data. Disagreement on whether analysis is optimally designed.

Perfect claim overlap on species differences (C95, C96). Both find SUPPORTED - OpenEval notes this as important caveat, peer reviewers explicitly requested discussion of discrepancies. Strong agreement on acknowledging limitations.

Both address G-CSF correlation (C72-C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with note that mechanism is speculative, peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without challenge. Agreement on correlation data, both acknowledge mechanistic speculation.

Both address MerTK expression (C101, C103). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting lack of functional efferocytosis assays, peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, questioning focus on T-cell rather than macrophage interactions. Agreement that functional validation is lacking.

Perfect claim overlap on chemotaxis (C105-C108). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with caveat about in vivo relevance, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, asking about S100A9 relevance for monocyte chemotaxis. Partial disagreement on mechanistic clarity.

Both address inflammatory markers (C109-C113, C114-C126). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for measurements and correlations, peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without challenge. Strong agreement on inflammatory marker data.

Large overlap on correlation data (C114-C126). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED noting correlations don't prove causality, peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED. Agreement on correlation validity with implicit understanding of limitations.

Both address monocyte subset differences (C34-C37). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on measurements, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting absolute numbers rather than percentages to support mobilization claims. Disagreement on data presentation adequacy.
Perfect claim overlap on T-cell subset distributions (C143-C147). Both find SUPPORTED - OpenEval notes importance of negative finding, peer reviewers accept without challenge. Strong agreement.

Perfect claim overlap on IL-12/IFN-γ association (C166). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on bioinformatic analysis, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, asking if IL-12 elevation is observed in patient plasma. Disagreement on whether in vivo validation is needed.

OpenEval finds lack of CD16/CD62L/CXCR4 distinction (C75-C78) SUPPORTED as important negative result. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - this characterization was not specifically addressed.

OpenEval finds CD10 marker utility and emergency granulopoiesis inference (C176-C178) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation - reviewers focused on specific data points rather than this synthesis.
OpenEval rates speculation about G-CSF therapy implications (C182, C194) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds characterization of proinflammatory properties (C192) SUPPORTED based on co-culture data. No corresponding peer review evaluation - covered implicitly in other assessments.
OpenEval rates IL-1β/monocyte recruitment speculation (C211, C221, C222) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds correlations between neutrophils and inflammatory markers (C216-C219) SUPPORTED with caveat about causality. No corresponding peer review evaluation - covered in broader correlation assessment.

OpenEval rates speculation about efferocytosis and apoptosis resistance consequences (C229, C233) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation - peer reviewers questioned related issues in R10.

OpenEval finds summary of expansion and proinflammatory role (C234-C236) SUPPORTED with speculation noted. No corresponding peer review evaluation - represents synthesis rather than specific data point.
